name: Junius Heights Special Purpose District
source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 397 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 397.

PD 397.

Junius Heights Special Purpose District

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 397 was established by Ordinance No. 22095, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 22, 1994. Ordinance No. 22095 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 22095; 25850)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 397 is established on property generally bounded by Abrams Road, Glasgow Drive, Reiger Avenue, Henderson Avenue, Dumas Street, and the alley at the rear of the lots on the southeast side of Gaston Avenue. The size of PD 397 is approximately 174.15 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22095; 25850)

sections.title: Purpose
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.103. PURPOSE.

The purpose of this PD is to encourage the future development of single family uses in the Junius Heights neighborhood. For this reason, limits on densities and the use of property have been imposed. Recognizing the need to promote the general welfare by conserving the value and unique architectural character of existing buildings in this area, however, the city council intends to: (1) allow existing small multifamily uses in this area to continue as conforming uses as long as they continuously operate in compliance with this article and the Dallas City Code, as amended, and (2) evaluate the appropriateness of large multifamily uses on a case-by-case basis. (Ord. Nos. 22095; 25850)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless the context clearly indicates otherwise, the definitions and provisions contained in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) MULTIFAMILY means seven or more dwelling units on a lot.

(2) QUADRAPLEX means four dwelling units on a lot.

(3) QUINPLEX means five dwelling units on a lot.

(4) SEXPLEX means six dwelling units on a lot.

(5) TRIPLEX means three dwelling units on a lot.

(6) VACANT LOT means a lot where there is no main use. A map that shows the vacant lots in this district as of June 22, 1994, is attached as Exhibit 397A.

(b) All references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district.

(d) The provisions of Section 51A-4.702, “Planned Development (PD) District Regulations,” do not apply to the establishment of this district. (Ord. Nos. 22095; 25850)

sections.title: Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.105. USES.

(a) Except as provided in Subsection (b), the uses permitted are as follows:

(1) Duplex.

(2) Triplex.

(3) Quadraplex.

(4) Quinplex.

(5) Sexplex.

(6) Multifamily. [SUP]

(7) Uses permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District. (For example, a use permitted in the R- 7.5(A) Single Family District by SUP only is permitted in this district by SUP only.)

(b) The following lots are limited exclusively to those uses permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District:

(1) Any vacant lot as of June 22, 1994.

(2) Any lot where the main building has been removed, demolished, or destroyed, or has been damaged such that the cost of repair is more than 60 percent of the cost of replacing the building as of the date it was damaged.

(3) Any lot where the use has been discontinued for six months or more. The board may grant a special exception to this provision only if the owner can show that there was a clear intent not to abandon the use even though the use was discontinued for six months or more.

(4) Any lot where the main building was found to be an urban nuisance and ordered demolished by the urban rehabilitation standards board under the provisions of Chapter 27 of the Dallas City Code, as amended, and all rights to appeal the decision of the board have been exhausted.

(c) Subsection (b) controls over Subsection (a) and the provisions of any ordinance granting an SUP for a multifamily use. (Ord. Nos. 22095; 25850)

sections.title: Density
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.106. DENSITY.

Except for a vacant lot, the number of dwelling units on a building site may not be increased. If the number of dwelling units in a building is reduced, or the building is replaced with another building containing fewer dwelling units, the building site must thereafter be limited to the lesser number of dwelling units. (Ord. Nos. 22095; 25850)

sections.title: Other Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.107. OTHER REGULATIONS.

Except as otherwise specified, the provisions for the R-7.5(A) Single Family District contained in Chapter 51A apply to this district. (Ord. Nos. 22095; 25850)

sections.title: Waiver Of Sup Fee
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.108. WAIVER OF SUP FEE.

The city council hereby waives the application fee for an SUP for a multifamily use for a period of one year from June 22, 1994. (Ord. Nos. 22095; 25850)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-397.109. ZONING MAP.

PD 397 is located on Zoning Map No. I-8. (Ord. Nos. 22095; 25850)
